idiom: to be on the same page
meaning: to agree or understand the same thing as other people
literal_translation: Estar na mesma página: concordar ou entender a mesma coisa que as outras pessoas
example: Let's check the plan again so we are all on the same page.
origin: Probably from people reading the same page of a document or book together

wrong_meanings.meaning: to open the same web page on two devices
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes a technical action, but the idiom is about agreement, not computers

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish reading a book before others
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is about speed of reading, not about sharing an understanding

wrong_meanings.meaning: to print a document for every employee
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes an office task, not the idea of agreeing or understanding together

explanation: 'To be on the same page' means that people agree or understand a situation in the same way. It is common in work and study when a team needs to share a plan.
